title: Technology Sector Update for 10/29/2018: RHT,IBM,YNDX,NXPI,TSEM
text:

Losses among technology stocks accelerated in afternoon trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing almost 3.3% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped over 2.7% shortly before today's closing bell.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Red Hat ( RHT ) soared Monday, rising as much as 49.5%, after the open-source software firm agreed to a $34 billion buyout offer from technology stalwart IBM ( IBM ). Under terms of the proposed transaction, expected to close in late 2019, Big Blue will pay $190 in cash for each Red Hat share, representing a $62.8% premium over Friday's closing price. IBM is expecting the deal to bolster its hybrid cloud offerings will add to its free cash flow and gross margin within 12 months after closing as well as accelerating future revenue growth and supporting an increased dividend. IBM shares were down almost 3% in late trade.
In other sector news:
(+) Yandex ( YNDX ) rose almost 6% at one point during Monday trading after the Russian language search engine company reported better-than-expected Q3 net income and revenue and raised its FY18 revenue outlook above Street views. Revenue jumped just under 39% to RUB32.57 billion from RUB23.44 billion during the same quarter last year to beat the Capital IQ consensus by RUB1.69 billion. Excluding one-time items, Yandex earned RUB15.25 per share, up from RUB2.72 per share last year and also topping the analyst mean expecting RUB14.25 per share.
(+) NXP Semiconductors NV ( NXPI ) added more than 4% during Monday trading after the chipmaker was selected to become a component company of the Nasdaq-100 Index, effective with the start of trading next Monday, Nov. 5. Along with the Nasdaq-100, NXP Semi also will join the Nasdaq-100 Equal Weighted and the Nasdaq-100 Technology Sector indices next week.
(-) Tower Semiconductor ( TSEM ) dropped as much as 18% on Monday after the semiconductor foundry company reported below-consensus Q3 financial results and upstaging an upbeat Q4 revenue forecast. Excluding one-time items, net income fell to $0.37 per share from $0.59 per share last year and trailing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.03 per share. Revenue also declined, dropping to $323 million from $354.6 million last year and missing Street views by $5 million.
